claims.claim: Prologue is a family paper about Seringapatam 1799
claims.evidence: 'The Storming of Seringapatam (1799): (Extracted from a Family Paper.)'
Prologue: 'a Yellow Diamond' among the treasure; storming of Seringapatam (not read to the seizure line in detail)

claims.claim: Story begins with Gabriel Betteredge, house-steward, 1848, citing Robinson Crusoe
claims.evidence: 'The Events related by Gabriel Betteredge, house-steward'; 'In the first part of Robinson Crusoe'

claims.claim: Diamond stolen from an Indian shrine
claims.evidence: Somnauth shrine, god of the Moon; epilogue 'in the forehead of the deity, gleamed the yellow Diamond'

claims.claim: Passes to Rachel on her eighteenth birthday
claims.evidence: 'My young lady's eighteenth birthday'; Colonel's will: 'I give and bequeath to my niece, Rachel Verinder'

claims.claim: Vanishes from her room that night
claims.evidence: Cuff's inquiry into the missing Diamond, Rachel's bedroom (Chapters on the loss)
'Miss Rachel has stolen her own Diamond?'

claims.claim: Rosanna loves Franklin and kills herself at Shivering Sand
claims.evidence: 'Rosanna has fallen in love with Mr. Franklin Blake'; 'Rosanna's suicide'; 'Shivering Sand is sucked down'

claims.claim: Rachel refuses to explain and breaks with Franklin
claims.evidence: 'I won't tell you!'; 'engagement is broken off'

claims.claim: Ezra Jennings is Mr. Candy's assistant
Franklin took the stone while drugged with opium
claims.evidence: 'You put the Diamond into his hand'; 'I can't take it back...My head's like lead' (Godfrey's account); Jennings's opium plan
'You put the Diamond into his hand. ... Take it back, Godfrey, to your father's bank.'
Luker offered to lend on pledge; 'Mr. Godfrey indignantly refused...Mr. Luker thereupon, handed him back the Diamond'

claims.claim: Godfrey is murdered by the Indians
claims.evidence: Report: 'moral, if not legal, evidence'; coroner: 'Wilful Murder against some person, or persons, unknown'; 'smothered Mr. Ablewhite'
claims.fix: Godfrey is smothered in a London lodging, and the evidence points to the Indians

claims.evidence: 'the marriage of Miss Rachel and Mr. Franklin Blake'
'in the forehead of the deity, gleamed the yellow Diamond'

claims.claim: Godfrey is Rachel's charming cousin, engaged to her
claims.evidence: 'Rachel's withdrawal from her engagement to him'

claims.claim: Betteredge is the Verinders' steward and first narrator
claims.evidence: 'house-steward in the service of Julia, Lady Verinder'
